headline: Live Vocabulary Upgrade Game for ESL Classes
problemStatement: Rote vocabulary drills produce passive learners who can define words but never use them. VocabSprint forces active, contextual word choice under pressure.
outcomes: Students replace weak words with stronger, more precise alternatives in real sentences
Build vocabulary depth by seeing words in authentic context rather than isolated lists
Develop speed and confidence choosing the right word under time pressure
Learn to distinguish word register and appropriateness for different situations
howItWorks: Teacher sets a topic — the AI generates a fresh set of sentences with deliberately weak or vague words
The current student reads the sentence on their device and types a stronger replacement word
AI evaluates the substitution for accuracy, precision, and contextual fit, then awards points
The class sees the result live on the board — the cycle repeats with a new sentence
teacherUseCases: Warm-up review after a unit on adjectives or verbs
End-of-unit consolidation before a writing assignment
Filler activity that still builds useful vocabulary muscle memory

faq.q: Can I use my own topic?
faq.a: Yes — type any topic into the session settings and the AI generates brand-new sentences on the fly. No pre-made content to prepare.

faq.q: How many students can play at once?
faq.a: Any class size works. With 3 or more students the game auto-switches to simultaneous mode where everyone submits answers and a race tracker shows who answered first.

faq.q: What devices do students use to play?
faq.a: Any phone or tablet with a browser works. Students type their answers on their own device and submit through a browser — no app download or account required.
Yes, LessonCaptain is free to try with no student account setup needed. Students join with a single link or code.

faq.q: What level is this suitable for?
faq.a: VocabSprint works well from A2 upward. You can adjust difficulty in session settings — easy rounds use simple sentences, hard rounds use more complex structures requiring nuanced word choices.

faq.q: Does the AI accept synonyms or only exact answers?
faq.a: The AI accepts any contextually appropriate word, not just a single 'correct' answer. Students are rewarded for precision and fit, so near-synonyms that work in context still earn points.
